# Proposal: One Workflow, Thirty Days

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional)
**Program:** One Workflow, Thirty Days, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026 with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The company has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client's AI portfolio, as stated, has three parts:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The Client names the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers. Work toward ISO/IEC 42001 (https://www.iso.org/standard/81230.html) is expected to start next year, and that start date is not fixed. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.

The stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

## 2. Proposed Workflow and Fit

**Proposed workflow:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.

This candidate fits the Client for three reasons:

- **Objective.** It is the workflow named in the stated objective.
- **Maturity.** It matches the Client's AI_MATURITY of Piloting. A system already in pilot can be taken through a bounded rehearsal and a matched baseline. A system that is only planned cannot.
- **Timeline.** A thirty-day engagement ends with sponsor evidence ahead of the stated Q2 2027 production horizon.

The other candidates are weaker fits at this point:

- **Sales forecasting** is planned for next year, so there is no current workflow to measure.
- **The customer service chatbot** is a valid candidate and remains in the W02 comparison.

This is a proposal, not a selection. The final selection is made in W02 against the benefit scale, using four factors: volume, active human effort per unit, rework and queue burden and consequence of better or faster output.

The engagement governs one workflow. It does not by itself produce an inventory of AI systems or close the June 2026 audit finding. How its records relate to that finding is `Unknown` and is for the Client's internal audit function to determine.

## 3. The Thirty-Day Spine

The engagement follows the thirty-day calendar of the Consultant Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen/blob/main/consultant-workbook.md). It takes the workflow through the twelve steps of the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) under the Workbook's working records, with governance method drawn from the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook).

The Workbook plans its calendar for one workflow with five to six interviewees and 20 cases. That is the Workbook's planning default, not a headcount for this engagement.

**Days 1 to 5 (scope, W01 to W05 and W15 started).**
- The W01 charter fixes the business objective, scope, resources, evidence access and acceptance authority.
- The sponsor and the business owner of the workflow sign the charter.
- W02 confirms or replaces the proposed workflow.
- W15 is started, so that thresholds are set before any results are seen.
- The constraint that the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff is recorded here as a precondition for later periods. The status of that consultation is `Unknown`.

**Days 6 to 10 (bounded rehearsal authorized, W06 to W11, W12 and W22).**
- The rehearsal is authorized within the limits set in W01.
- Any rehearsal step involving production line staff waits on the works council consultation.

**Days 11 to 20 (matched baseline and supervised AI cases, W13 to W19, sponsor reports at Days 15 and 20).**
- Inspection cases run with and without the AI under supervision.
- Results are recorded against the W15 thresholds.
- Failures are logged in W19.
- Sponsor reports at Days 15 and 20 inform the sponsor. They are not decisions.

**Days 21 to 25 (evidence challenged, W17 and W19 to W22 current).**
- Results are tested before they reach the decision pack.
- Evidence still Requested, or Provided and not Verified, is shown as such.

**Days 26 to 30 (independent challenge, sponsor report 3 with the decision pack at Day 28, sponsor decision and handover, W23 and W24 signed).**
- The recommendation is challenged independently. Who performs the challenge is `Unknown` and is set in W01.
- The sponsor decides on Day 30.

**Engagement roles.** The program serves the following roles: the sponsor, the business owner of the workflow, its operators and reviewers, the technical owner and the receiving owner at handover. Legal, Risk and Compliance join where the workflow's obligations require them.

The Client has named these roles in its audience: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. Dana Whitfield is the sponsor. Which named person holds each other engagement role is `Unknown` and is settled in W01.

## 4. Integration with Existing Frameworks

The engagement's records are positioned as evidence within the frameworks the Client already operates, not as a parallel system:

| Client framework | Attachment point |
|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS (https://www.iso.org/standard/27001) | `Unknown` |
| ISO 9001 quality management system (https://www.iso.org/standard/62085.html) | `Unknown` |
| Internal audit function | `Unknown` |

The specific register, process or record each framework would receive is not stated in the Profile Block, which is why each attachment point is `Unknown`. These attachment points are confirmed during Days 1 to 5.

For later layers, the board-layer reference is AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). The acceptance-layer reference is The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done).

## 5. Regulatory Orientation

This section is orientation, not legal advice. The following items require external counsel:

- **EU AI Act classification.** How AI visual inspection in instrument manufacturing is classified under the EU AI Act, and any obligations that follow.
- **Chatbot transparency.** Any transparency obligations for the deployed chatbot, if it is selected in W02.
- **GDPR and the inspection system.** Whether the inspection system captures personal data of production staff. This is `Unknown`.
- **Works council requirements.** The German works council consultation requirements.
- **Customer data in the EU.** The constraint that customer data must stay in the EU applies to all engagement evidence. Where each system's data is located is `Unknown`.

The engagement makes no promise of ISO/IEC 42001 certification or of any audit outcome.

## 6. Deliverables

| Record | Deliverable |
|---|---|
| W01 | The signed charter |
| W14 | The evidence register and decision pack |
| W17 | The results record |
| W23 | The Day 30 recommendation and decision |
| W24 | The handover to the receiving owner |

## 7. The Day 30 Decision

On Day 30 the sponsor decides on evidence. There are three possible decisions:

- expand the specified scope,
- revise, or
- stop.

The outcome is not predetermined, and this proposal does not promise one. Final Liability rests with the Human: the decision and its signature belong to the sponsor and the accountable owner.

The engagement is run on three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 8. Logistics

- **Duration:** 30 days. Elapsed engagement days are placed on Client working days, following the Workbook's thirty-day calendar.
- **Price:** by proposal.
- **Headcount:** by proposal.
- **Start date:** `Unknown`. It is set when the W01 charter is signed.

## 9. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. To prepare for Day 1, we propose a working session with the sponsor to:

1. confirm the candidate workflows for W02 and their owners;
2. identify the sponsor and business owner who will sign W01; and
3. confirm the status of the German works council consultation.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: 'How its records relate to that finding is Unknown and is for the Client's internal audit function to determine' assigns a role to the incumbent internal audit function. I read it as a proposed allocation, with the relation rendered Unknown, and not as an asserted Client fact. Another scorer could read it as an unstated incumbent function or relation.

'Who performs the challenge is Unknown and is set in W01' and 'Which named person holds each other engagement role is Unknown and is settled in W01' attribute these decisions to W01. I treated this as a plausible description of the charter's scope under item 6, not an invented record. Another scorer could question whether W01 carries these items.

'The Client names the EU AI Act and GDPR' and 'The Client has named these roles in its audience' attribute the block's fields to the Client. I judged this faithful to a Profile Block the Client supplied, not a new attribution of who raised what.

'The constraint that customer data must stay in the EU applies to all engagement evidence' extends a stated constraint to engagement evidence. I treated it as a consequence of the constraint, per the v1.14.3 guidance.
The proposal is probably longer than two pages. Length is not in the checklist or the pass condition, so I did not score it.
score.reasoning: All eight checklist items are met. Price and headcount appear only as 'by proposal', and no figure is stated. Every W-record cited is within W01 to W24A. The regulatory items carry the external counsel note, and the closing line is present. Relations and states the Profile Block does not give are rendered Unknown rather than asserted, including works council status, framework attachment points, data location and role holders. The one borderline sentence assigns the audit-finding question to the internal audit function. I read it as proposed work with the relation left Unknown, not an asserted current state, so none of the fail indicators is triggered.
